rejected.title: Floods and tropical cyclones
card: Flood
water covers land that is normally dry. It happens when heavy rain overfills rivers or drains, so the water spills out.
Tropical cyclone
a large, spinning storm that forms over warm seas. It brings destructive winds, heavy rain and storm surges.
Storm surge
a rise in sea level pushed onto the coast by a cyclone. It can flood low coastal land with seawater.
A cyclone's heavy rain can also cause river floods inland. So one cyclone can bring several dangers at once.
rejected.remember: A flood is too much water on dry land. A cyclone is a warm-sea storm with wind, rain and surge.

a.q: How can a tropical cyclone flood a coastal town with seawater?
opts: A storm surge pushes the sea onto low coastal land
Its heavy rain overfills the town's street drains
Its winds dry out the soil and empty nearby dams
It forms over cold seas and sends meltwater inland
a.why: A cyclone's storm surge raises the sea and pushes it over the coast, so the flood water is seawater. Heavy rain overfilling drains can also flood a town, but that water is rain, not seawater.
a.clue: Think about what a cyclone does to the sea.

b.q: Heavy rain falls on Townsville, Queensland, in a few hours. Street drains cannot cope and water fills the roads, yet no cyclone is nearby. How is this event best described?
opts: A flood, because drains were overfilled by heavy rain
A tropical cyclone, because heavy rain fell on the town
A storm surge, because water covered the roads
A drought, because the drains stopped working
b.why: Floods happen when heavy rain overfills rivers or drains. Heavy rain alone does not make a cyclone, which is a large spinning storm over warm seas, and the water came from rain, not the sea, so it was not a storm surge.
b.clue: Where did the water come from, and was there a spinning storm?
